newsitem.title: GERMANY: German share market ends at all-time closing high.
newsitem.headline: German share market ends at all-time closing high.

text.p: The German share market rallied strongly during low-volume trade on Monday to end on an record closing high, shrugging off fears of a fall after a surprise left-wing win in the first round of French elections.
The IBIS DAX, which tracks electronic trade in 30 German blue-chips, ended the day at 3,669.31 points, up 47.59 points or 1.31 percent -- an all-time closing high.
The index's previous record high was 3,627.43 points. The IBIS DAX reached its highest-ever level at 3,676.87 points late in the afternoon.
Earlier the DAX index ended floor trade up 55.67 points, or 1.55 percent, at 3,657.86 points.

"Volumes are relatively thin today, but we were surprised to see this performance after the result from France this morning. We expected a consolidation with that kind of news," said one Frankfurt trader.
The market had fallen earlier after the news from France, but as another dealer said -- "Political events never have a long-lasting effect on markets."
Traders did see the win for the left as a strong warning shot for the ruling conservatives, but were unsure whether or not the trend would continue.

Market holidays in the United States and Britain capped market volumes over the day. These holidays, combined with a lack of new information on fundamentals and the weaker, albeit stable, dollar against the mark, meant that trade was quiet, albeit never far off record territory.
A star performer was the chemical sector which acted as the engine for the stock market's advance.
Sentiment was boosted by news that Swiss pharmaceutical group Roche Holding AG had bought the privately-held German pharmaceutical and diagnostics group Boehringer Mannheim.
"I don't really know why this has boosted the chemicals, as this acquisition means new competition from Roche for Hoechst AG and Bayer AG," said a trader.
"But it does show that the concentration process is continuing and the markets like that," he said.
BASF ended up 1.65 marks, or 2,56 percent, at 66.15 marks, while Bayer ended up 1.75 marks, or 2.62 percent, at 68.65 marks. Hoechst ended up 1.17 marks, or 1.71 percent, at 69.52.

"The markets are generally a little bit scared when New York and London are both closed, so while we are up at higher levels today, with thin volumes, we could see a bump down tomorrow," a trader said.
